title: India extends 95% RELIEF export risk cover to March 31, 2027
summary:
India's Department of Commerce has extended RELIEF Component II until March 31, 2027, citing West Asia maritime disruption.
The measure offers 95 per cent ECGC risk coverage for eligible Standalone and Whole Turnover Policies obtained on or after March 16, 2026.
It covers FCL, LCL and reefer containers, excluding energy shipments; claims are filed through ECGC's customer portal.

title: North India’s cotton yarn market stable, liquidity remains tight
summary:
North India cotton yarn prices stayed stable as weak demand and payment constraints curbed trade in Ludhiana and Delhi; Panipat remained sluggish.
Traders expect Diwali garment and home textile sales to improve liquidity, restocking and spinning mill cash flow.
Cotton held steady despite weaker ICE trends; mills avoided bulk buying and north India's crop is seen at 26-28 lakh bales.

title: PTA, polyester melt prices down in India; mixed trend in China
summary:
India’s polyester raw material prices fell further in the October 24 revision, with PTA and polyester melt reduced while MEG stayed unchanged.
Since October 10, PTA has dropped ₹3.90 (~$0.04) per kg, MEG ₹7 per kg and polyester melt ₹5.74 per kg, extending a domestic correction.
CFR China PTA rose $25 per tonne during October 19-23, while MEG gained $5 amid Asian petrochemical volatility.

title: Turkiye's GDP growth averages 5.5% over 23 years
summary:
Turkiye averaged 5.5 per cent annual GDP growth over the past 23 years under President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, despite regional geopolitical crises, Necmeddin Bilal Erdogan said at the Verona Eurasian Economic Forum in Istanbul.
He said Turkiye seeks to shape a multipolar world order, leads in per-capita humanitarian aid and offers Istanbul as a hub for international conferences.

title: India-NZ FTA: Can zero tariffs boost $125.6 mn in textile exports?
summary:
India-New Zealand FTA took effect on October 20, 2026, eliminating duties on all 8,284 New Zealand tariff lines for qualifying Indian goods, including textiles, apparel and carpets.
Some lines earlier faced tariffs of up to 10 per cent, but benefits depend on HS-code tariffs and rules of origin; TexPro puts New Zealand’s 2025 imports of Indian textiles and apparel at $125.6 million.

title: US producer prices rise 6.3%, fastest since 2022
summary:
US producer prices rose 6.3 per cent year-on-year in September 2026, the fastest annual increase since December 2022, while the monthly index climbed 1.3 per cent, its biggest rise since March 2022. 
Energy costs drove the increase, with final-demand energy prices surging 10.8 per cent and gasoline prices jumping 20.3 per cent.

title: Euro area deficit rises to 3.3% of GDP in Q2 2026
summary:
Euro area seasonally adjusted general government deficit rose to 3.3 per cent of GDP in Q2 2026 from 3.2 per cent in Q1, while the EU ratio increased to 3.5 per cent from 3.1 per cent. 
Eurostat said euro area revenue eased to 46.8 per cent of GDP and expenditure rose to 50.1 per cent. 
EU revenue was 46.3 per cent of GDP and expenditure 49.8 per cent; Q1 and Q2 data are provisional.

title: Germany's producer prices rise 6.7% in September, fastest since 2023
summary:
German industrial producer prices rose 6.7 per cent year on year in September 2026, the largest increase since March 2023, driven by a 14.9 per cent surge in energy costs. 
Mineral oil product prices jumped 51.3 per cent, while intermediate goods rose 6.4 per cent. 
Excluding energy, producer prices increased 3.2 per cent. 
Non-durable consumer goods prices fell 1.8 per cent, led by lower food prices.

title: IMF forecasts uneven recovery across Middle East & Central Asia
summary:
IMF projects MENAP to contract by about 1.3 per cent in 2026 before rebounding 6.6 per cent in 2027, as conflict disrupts energy, shipping, trade and tourism. 
It cut the 2026 forecast by 2.7 percentage points, with Gulf oil exporters hit hardest while oil importers show resilience. 
CCA growth is seen at 5.2 per cent in 2026, but logistics costs, food prices and downside risks remain elevated.

title: India & Germany discuss trade & technology ties in Berlin
summary:
India’s Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has concluded a two-day Germany visit, with Berlin talks focused on trade, investment, advanced manufacturing, research and emerging technologies. 
He met German Federal Chancellery adviser Levin Holle and leaders from Siemens Healthineers, Bertelsmann and Volkswagen. 
Indian delegates joined sectoral roundtables with German industry.

title: Canada's Gildan completes $490 mn HanesBrands Australia sale
summary:
Canada's Gildan Activewear has completed the sale of HanesBrands Australia to BBFIT Investments for approximately Au$700 million ($490 million) in cash. 
The company plans to use the net proceeds to repay outstanding debt. 
The divestment supports Gildan's ongoing integration strategy, with a focus on operational priorities, capturing synergies and strengthening its portfolio of brands.

title: Bangladesh garment workers’ council demands $260 minimum monthly wage
summary:
IndustriALL Bangladesh Council has demanded a $260 monthly minimum wage for Bangladesh garment workers, citing higher living costs and market volatility.
IBC said essentials, transport and medical costs had strained workers, alongside a 100 to 142 per cent rise for government employees.
It plans grade-wise wage proposals once the full wage board is formed.

title: Could Suez reopen in 2027 and cut costs for EU apparel?
summary:
Europe’s apparel supply chain may see most container lines return to the Suez Canal by early second quarter 2027, but lower freight bills are not assured.
TexPro says the EU imported $23.08 billion of selected cotton-heavy apparel from Bangladesh, China, India and Vietnam in 2025.
Demand weakness and capacity management could keep delivered costs under pressure for garment buyers.

title: Myanmar's apparel export dependence shifts from Europe to Asia
summary:
Myanmar's apparel exports fell 21.1 per cent year on year to $3.757 billion in January–September 2026, with Europe's share down to 53.57 per cent.
Europe-bound shipments dropped 25.1 per cent to $2.013 billion, while Asia-Pacific's share rose to 36.18 per cent after a milder decline.
Japan led destinations at $852.863 million, ahead of Germany, Poland, South Korea and Italy.

title: Jordan's apparel exports rise 2.9% to $1.45 bn in Jan–July 2026
summary:
Jordan's apparel exports rose 2.9 per cent year on year to JOD 1.029 billion (~$1.45 billion) in January–July 2026, data showed.
Knitted apparel drove growth, up 4.1 per cent and representing 98.2 per cent of clothing exports, while woven exports fell 37.6 per cent.
July clothing exports grew 8.5 per cent, helping the sector outperform national exports; apparel imports rose 4.7 per cent.

title: Canada's Lululemon appoints Tara Poseley to board of directors
summary:

Poseley, most recently CEO of Paula’s Choice Skincare, joins under the company’s cooperation agreement with founder Dennis “Chip” Wilson and brings more than 30 years of retail, apparel and beauty experience.

title: Brazil’s 0% parcel duty: Is local apparel paying the price?
summary:
Brazil’s 0 per cent federal duty for qualifying Remessa Conforme purchases up to $50 remains current policy under Law 15,502, but rates can change.
Purchases outside the programme generally face 60 per cent duty; state ICMS of 17–20 per cent still applies.
Remittance declarations rose 73.8 per cent in August 2026, while apparel output fell 10.6 per cent; causation is not established.

title: EU seizes record 196 mn counterfeits worth $7.1 bn; clothing tops list
summary:
EU authorities seized a record 196 million counterfeit items worth €6.3 billion ($7.1 billion) in 2025, up 67 per cent from 2024, the European Commission said. 
Clothing accounted for nearly one-fifth of detained items. 
Customs intercepted 42 million goods at EU borders, with most cases linked to express courier and postal shipments associated with e-commerce.

title: Bangladesh apparel exports to EU fall 11.4%: What drives the drop?
summary:
TexPro data show Bangladesh apparel export value for HS 61 and HS 62 to EU destinations fell 11.43 per cent in January–August 2026.
Values declined 4.31 per cent to the United States, 0.61 per cent to the United Kingdom and 7.69 per cent worldwide.
Eurostat data show EU apparel imports from Bangladesh fell 11.67 per cent; buyers should prepare for the EU’s post-transition preference framework.

title: US’ Deckers Brands' Q2 profit rises 17% as Hoka, UGG expand
summary:

Second-quarter net sales rose 3.5 per cent to $1.48 billion, while net income increased 17 per cent to $313.1 million.
